stem.en: A Very Large Crude Carrier waits outside a shallow part of the Singapore Strait. What is it waiting for?

text.en: A calm day, so that the wind cannot turn it

feedback.en: No. The problem is the depth of the water under the hull.

text.en: Low tide, so that the tidal current has stopped

feedback.en: No. Low tide leaves the least water over the shallow part.

text.en: Full moon, so that the crew can see at night

feedback.en: No. It is waiting for water, not for light.

text.en: High tide, so that it has water under its hull

feedback.en: Yes. It crosses at high tide so that it does not run aground.

explanation.en: A ship can cross only where the water is deeper than its draught. High tide adds water over the shallow part, so a VLCC often waits for hours and crosses only then.

hints.en: The ship's draught stays the same. What else can change?
